title: Egg Size Variation Between Wild and Captive Broodstock Brown Trout (Salmo trutta) in Watersheds of Three Peri‐Alpine Lakes
content:
This study examined variations in the egg size of wild-caught and captive broodstock (created from the direct offspring of wild-caught) brown trout (Salmo trutta) from three peri-Alpine lakes (Lake Constance, Lake Lucerne and Lake Zurich). It showed that there was lake-specific variation in egg size between the two groups of trout. Specifically, captive broodstock trout produced slightly smaller eggs than wild-caught trout in Lakes Lucerne and Zurich, but not in Lake Constance.


ABSTRACT

Captive environments could lead to plastic and/or heritable shifts in key life-history traits, such as egg size. Although many studies have examined how egg size differs between wild and captive females, the results are mixed. Therefore, system-specific studies on egg size variation are valuable. In the present study, we examined how wild-caught and captive broodstock brown trout (Salmo trutta) differ in egg size using eggs from three peri-Alpine lakes (Lake Constance, Lake Lucerne and Lake Zurich). In addition to clutch-mean egg size, which has been extensively studied traditionally, we also focused on the degree of within-clutch variation. There was no significant difference in the degree of within-clutch variation between wild-caught and captive broodstock females across the lake watersheds. However, variation in clutch-mean egg size between wild-caught and captive broodstock females differed among the lake watersheds. Specifically, captive broodstock females produced eggs slightly smaller than those of wild-caught females in Lakes Lucerne and Zurich. In contrast, wild-caught and captive broodstock females produced eggs of similar size in Lake Constance. Future studies elucidating the mechanisms underlying variation in egg size between wild-caught and captive broodstock females and across lake watersheds are essential for a better understanding of the consequences of stocking programmes for wild brown trout populations in the watersheds of peri-Alpine lakes.
